notes:
THE MISSED 200th. Every other row got a speaker plan on 2026-07-18; this one
never did, so run_batch never saw it and the video Cameron has been watching
still carries the pre-SPEAKER-LAW narration. The speaker assignments below were
already applied by hand to make_narration.py -- this file records them so the
build is reproducible and can never be skipped again.

GREEN, not red: Exodus is Old Testament, so every line the Lord speaks here is
premortal Jehovah -- GOD, green. A red-letter Bible prints none of Exodus 33 in
red, and the doctrine section of SPEAKER-LAW.md is explicit that green is how
these videos carry premortal Christ.
  g14  Exodus 33:14  'My presence shall go with thee...'
  g19  Exodus 33:19  'I will make all my goodness pass before thee...'
  g20  Exodus 33:20  'Thou canst not see my face...'

BLUE: s18 is Moses asking, so it is a man quoted from the KJV -- SCRIPTURE.
sface is Exodus 33:11 quoted as narration of the text rather than someone
speaking, and it stays SCRIPTURE for the same reason.

NO WOMEN: Exodus 33 records no woman speaking.

WHY-LAW: God talks with a man the way a man talks with his friend, then hides
him in a rock to keep him safe from too much glory. Milk framing -- nearness first, majesty second.

IDS: the original build.py beats are nface/jv14/jv19/jv20 and the music beds
and start_of[] lookups key off them, so they keep their names even though
nface is now blue and the jv* beats are now green. A hand pass had renamed them
to sface/g14/g19/g20 and migrate refused the plan outright.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Moses pitched a tent a little way outside the camp and called it the Tent of Meeting. It was the place he went to be with God — set apart, quiet, away from everything else.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Whenever Moses walked out to that tent, something happened that had never happened for anyone.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: All the people would rise and stand, each at the door of their own tent, and watch him go, and worship — because they knew where he was going, and who was waiting for him there.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As Moses reached the tent, a great pillar of cloud would come down and stand at the door — the presence of God himself, come down to meet one man.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: And the LORD spake unto Moses face to face, as a man speaketh unto his friend.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Face to face. As a man speaks with his friend. Not a master barking at a servant. Not a king across a vast throne room — easy, honest, close. God wanted Moses. Not just his obedience. His friendship.

segments.speaker: god
segments.text: My presence shall go with thee, and I will give thee rest.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: I will go with you myself, and I will give you rest. Not send someone ahead. Not watch from somewhere far off. Go with you.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And that friendship made Moses bold. He asked for the one thing no one had ever dared to ask.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: I beseech thee, shew me thy glory.

segments.speaker: god
segments.text: I will make all my goodness pass before thee, and I will proclaim the name of the LORD before thee.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Show me your glory, Moses asked. And God answered — I will make all my goodness pass in front of you. Not his power. Not his greatness. His goodness. Of everything he could have shown a friend, that is what he chose.

segments.speaker: god
segments.text: Thou canst not see my face: for there shall no man see me, and live.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: You cannot see my face and live. That was not a refusal. It was care — the way you would not hand a child something far too heavy to hold.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So God did the gentlest thing. He tucked Moses into a cleft in the rock, and covered him with his own hand, and let all his goodness pass by — near enough to feel, too much to look on. He protected his friend even from the weight of his own glory.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And when Moses came back down, his face was shining. He did not even know it.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: That is what happens to someone who spends time close to God — you start, quietly, to glow with a little of him. It began with a friendship, at a tent, outside the camp.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: God spoke with a man as with a friend, and hid him in a rock to keep him safe from too much glory. He still wants to be known like that — not feared from far off, but known up close. Would you let him be that kind of friend to you?
